LESSON 12

even though entangled in the evil system through ignorance. It is wrong for men to attempt to build a church, to form a religious doctrine, or to rule the people of God. The chief wrong in these is substituting human rule for divine rule. All such is doomed to destruction. A list of the terrible penalties for Babylon is recorded in verses 21-24 of this chapter. Her sins have reached unto heaven. There the record will be opened at the Judgment.
No Other Gospel

Galatians 1:8-12 There is no other gospel, no other true doctrine, than that which Paul preached, which is the Gospel found in the New Testament. Why is it the only one? Because it is not after man. It was not Paul who was persuading men, that is, not in his own ability or his authority. God was doing it through him. The Gospel Paul preached was not man-made. Paul was not told it by man or educated into it. It is by the revelation of Jesus Christ. Jesus revealed it to him. There is but one revealed and supernatural Gospel from God. This Gospel ONLY can be rightfully passed on—unchanged, with no additions or subtractions. This is so important that a curse is pronounced against any who teach or preach another (Revelation 22:19).
Strange Plants to Be Rooted Up

Matthew 15:13 Jesus was condemning the Pharisees' traditions and commandments of men. Then, Every plant, which my heavenly Father hath not planted—every doctrine, rule, theory, creed, system, or organization not from God—shall be rooted up. What then will be the fate of those entangled in the humanly planted plants?

The difference is also in the authority behind the church. The Church of God has the authority of God. Human organizations depend upon the authority of men. The church takes the authority of God's Word, the Bible. Human organizations take that of their leaders, councils, conferences, creeds, disciplines, doctrines, traditions, etc. They may say, "Christ is our Head." Why, then, have a man as head? Anything with two heads is a freak, a monstrosity. What man has the right to take in or put out members, to write creeds, to negotiate doctrines, changes, and mergers?
Counterfeit

A counterfeit dollar bill may look real, but it was not made by the government. A counterfeit church is any not authorized by Christ and which places human authority where divine ought to be. Since one enters the Church of God by spiritual birth, any group one can enter by joining can only be a counterfeit.

One may say, "I know people who belong to a certain denomination who are just as godly and filled with the Spirit as anyone can be." Certainly. They look to God and His Word as their authority. They open their hearts to Him. They belong to Him. These are the ones to whom Christ calls, Come out of her, my people, and stand in Me alone. God desires His people to come out of her, and to stay out.

In these days, we are hearing much about an ecumenical movement which is attempting to build a one-world church by uniting all denominations regardless of their belief. It includes the Word keepers, and they are blind to the fact that Christ has already built a one-world church. It is the body of Christ. (Read Colossians 1:18, 24.) There will never be another. There will never be a need for one, for the Church of God will never be destroyed. (See Matthew 16:18.) Any other can be only a counterfeit. A humanly built church is a human church that is all. It is only a religious organization—natural, not supernatural. Such will have union but will lack unity. No mechanical union can produce spiritual unity. The difference is in the life which empowers the church. The Church of God is the household of God, and her members are fellowcitizens . . . God keeps her membership (Ephesians 2:19-22; 2 Timothy 2:19). They depart from iniquity—live holy.

paragraphs.text: In these days, we are hearing much about an ecumenical movement which is attempting to build a one-world church by uniting all denominations regardless of their belief. It includes the Word keepers, and they are blind to the fact that Christ has already built a one-world church. It is the body of Christ. (Read Colossians 1:18, 24.) There will never be another. There will never be a need for one, for the Church of God will never be destroyed. (See Matthew 16:18.) Any other can be only a counterfeit. A humanly built church is a human church that is all. blocks.text: SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 13
A SUPERNATURAL RESURRECTION
Scripture Texts: John 6:38-40; 1 Corinthians 15:19-23, 1 Corinthians
15:35-38, 1 Corinthians 15:42-56; 1 Thessalonians 4:13-18.

We have been studying of the good things Jesus prepared in this world for His people. Today we look at some of the things He has prepared for His people in the next world. They are all supernatural. After a person has finished a saved life here in this world, what then? Jesus promised that He was going to the Father, to Heaven, where He had been in the beginning. He said He was going back to the Father, and that each saint could go also. He prayed that those given Him would be with Him in His glory (John 17).

No one can reach Heaven by natural power or goodness. Only the life of God within a person takes him to Heaven. Heaven is a condition as well as a place. Wherever the location of Heaven, it will be where Jesus is and under His love and protection. To really know Jesus, to have Him living within, is the only way to Heaven.
MEMORY VERSE: And this is the will of him that sent me, that every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day. —John 6:40
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—1 Corinthians 15:16-34 Certainty of the Resurrection.
Tue.—1 Corinthians 15:35-58 Explanation of Resurrection.
Wed.—2 Corinthians 5:1-10 Blessings of Heaven are real.
Thu.—1 Thessalonians 5:1-11 Watching for Christ's coming.
Fri.—1 Peter 1:1-9 Hope of Heaven by Christ's Resurrection.
Devotional Reading: Philippians 3:8-21 Our bodies to be like His.
Resurrection Promised

John 6:38-40 That of all which he hath given me . . . All must come to Jesus Christ through the Father . . . may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day. This promise from Jesus is that all the saved will have a supernatural passage to Heaven. Salvation transforms a person from the first death to new spiritual life in the first resurrection. There is no transformation of the spirit after the second death. Eternal life is not obtained at death; it is received and begun in this life and continues on after death in Heaven. We must have forgiveness of sin, or we perish eternally. The life of the lost will also go on forever; that is what makes it so terrible. But the destiny of the lost is not what the Bible refers to as everlasting life. Everlasting life speaks better of its quality than of its duration.
The Glory of the Resurrection

1 Corinthians 15:19-23 Now is Christ risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that slept. Jesus was our example in all things, so we will rise from the dead as He did. Afterward they that are Christ's at his coming.

1 Corinthians 15:35-38 Here in these verses we are told that the glory of planting a seed compares to the Resurrection. One does not expect to get back only the seed planted, but the seed planted must die and be quickened to come forth in a glorious manner. One seed is planted, and it dies and comes forth a more glorious body, bearing the same grain, but with greater glory than that which was planted. How? But God giveth it a
© 2015 Church of God, Inc. A Supernatural Resurrection─ Lesson 13 www.GodsAcres.org
SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 13
body . . . The soul was made for God, and only God and His Spirit can satisfy it and prepare it to come forth in glory.
The Triumph of the Resurrection

1 Corinthians 15:42-56 The dead is sown in corruption—a mortal body. It is raised in incorruption—an immortal body. It is sown in dishonor—it goes back to the dust from which it came. It is raised in glory— never to die again, but to go back to God Who gave it. The natural man was first, then the spiritual man. As transformed man had an earthly body's image, so also will he have a heavenly body's image. We shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed. Here Paul attempts to explain the supernatural phase of the Resurrection. In a moment—very quickly—at the last trump—no more preaching or time for preparation—for the trumpet shall sound—awakening all that are dead, wherever their graves are. And the dead shall be raised incorruptible—every grave will bring forth an incorruptible body and shall be changed.
After the Funeral, What Then?

1 Thessalonians 4:13-14 All of us experience death. We sorrow for departed ones. But some sorrow with hope, some without hope. The difference is that some die in Christ, some outside of Him. If we believe . . . As surely as Christ's death and resurrection are true facts, so also the resurrection of God's people is true. Because He lives, we shall live also (John 14:19). Physical death is called a sleep, a sleep of the body. It is not the end of existence. Nothing is destroyed. Death is a change, a separation of soul and body. But one thing does not change at death—one's spiritual relationship. Those who live in Christ sleep in Jesus. Just as truly, those who live without Him die without Him, and so without hope. By what means will God raise His people to eternal life? Shall raise up us also by Jesus—by his Spirit that dwelleth in you. (Read 2 Corinthians 4:14 and Romans 8:11.) In the same way that He raised Jesus, by the presence of God dwelling in them. Them also which sleep in Jesus will God bring with him. Those who died having the Spirit of Christ will go to be with Jesus. Then Jesus will bring their spirits to be reunited with their resurrected bodies. In these modern times some try to cover death with a screen of beauty. Some try to ignore it with pain-killing, sleep-inducing drugs before death, flowers, music, and poetry afterward. But death remains real and universal. God calls it an enemy in 1 Corinthians 15:26 and refers to death in Hebrews 9:27. Words of friends, sympathy cards, and funeral sermons largely imply that the departed one will go to Heaven. But it requires something more, something from each individual, if one is to be with God.
The Manner of the Resurrection

1 Thessalonians 4:15-18 Paul spoke by the word of the Lord. This is God's Word, not Paul's. (1) We which are alive and remain . . . shall not prevent them which are asleep. Notice the only people spoken of here are saints, those who have died, and those still alive at Christ's coming. Those who died in sin are not addressed here. (2) The Lord himself shall descend—He will be seen. With a shout—He will be heard. With the trump of God—all will be awakened. (3) The dead in Christ shall rise first. The dead saints will be resurrected first. Then we which are alive—saints who have not yet died—shall be caught up together with them in the clouds. Those souls who have died without Christ will not be in this supernatural reunion. The dead in Christ from all ages shall come forth from the graves with new immortal bodies, along with those still living. (4) Where will all go? To meet the Lord in the air, and to ever be with the Lord, eternally, time without end, never again separated from Him. Paul was giving hope to the brethren of all ages. The wicked will be resurrected at the same time, but to a sadly different destiny (John 5:28-29).

From our studies we learn that supernaturally saved people will be supernaturally resurrected, supernaturally changed to be immortal, caught up by supernatural power to meet the supernatural Lord, and taken to dwell in a

supernaturally prepared place. We can never take ourselves to Heaven, but Jesus can, all because of His supernatural resurrection.

The natural man was first, then the spiritual man.
As transformed man had an earthly body's image, so also will he have a heavenly body's image.
We shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed.
Here Paul attempts to explain the supernatural phase of the Resurrection.
In a moment—very quickly—at the last trump—no more preaching or time for preparation—for the trumpet shall sound—awakening all that are dead, wherever their graves are.
And the dead shall be raised incorruptible—every grave will bring forth an incorruptible body and shall be changed.

paragraphs.text: 1 Thessalonians 4:13-14 All of us experience death. We sorrow for departed ones. But some sorrow with hope, some without hope. The difference is that some die in Christ, some outside of Him. If we believe . . . As surely as Christ's death and resurrection are true facts, so also the resurrection of God's people is true. Because He lives, we shall live also (John 14:19). Physical death is called a sleep, a sleep of the body. It is not the end of existence. Nothing is destroyed. Death is a change, a separation of soul and body. But one thing does not change at death—one's spiritual relationship. Those who live in Christ sleep in Jesus. Just as truly, those who live without Him die without Him, and so without hope. By what means will God raise His people to eternal life? Shall raise up us also by Jesus—by his Spirit that dwelleth in you. (Read 2 Corinthians 4:14 and Romans 8:11.) In the same way that He raised Jesus, by the presence of God dwelling in them. Them also which sleep in Jesus will God bring with him. Those who died having the Spirit of Christ will go to be with Jesus. Then Jesus will bring their spirits to be reunited with their resurrected bodies. In these modern times some try to cover death with a screen of beauty. Some try to ignore it with pain-killing, sleep-inducing drugs before death, flowers, music, and poetry afterward. But death remains real and universal. God calls it an enemy in 1 Corinthians 15:26 and refers to death in Hebrews 9:27. Words of friends, sympathy cards, and funeral sermons largely imply that the departed one will go to Heaven. But it requires something more, something from each individual, if one is to be with God.

lines.text: SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 1
SUPERNATURAL ORIGIN
Scripture Text: Genesis 2:7-20
The fact that God made man and placed him here is the
foundation of religion. This fact puts us in relationship with God.
God created man. Therefore, He has authority over all people. This
is the basis of salvation, or man's relationship with the true and
living God. God prescribes the manner of that relationship. This
makes it a supernatural religion, one given and administered by
God. No one can escape this relationship. Every person is responsible to God. As all Creation is of God's plan
and work, so salvation, or Creation's relationship with God, is God's plan. Any other plan is a false religion.
In this quarter we will study and attempt to clarify why God's religion is completely supernatural. This is
why man cannot arrange his own manner of worship.
MEMORY VERSE: And when Abram was ninety years old and nine, the LORD appeared to Abram, and said
unto him, I am the Almighty God; walk before me, and be thou perfect.
—Genesis 17:1
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—Genesis 1:26-31 Creation of man.
Tue.—Deuteronomy 30:8-20 Duty to obey God.
Wed.—Psalm 119:89-96 God's unchangeable Law.
Thu.—Romans 14:7-13 We must give account to God.
Fri.—1 Corinthians 3:16-23 Man made for God's dwelling.
Devotional Reading: Psalm 24 Our responsibility to God.
A Supernatural Creation
Genesis 2:7 The Lord God formed man of the dust . . . breath of life . . . living soul. The materials were
already created; now from some of them, God formed man. This is the origin of the whole human race. The
beasts also were made of the ground (verse 19). Only man is made in the image of God, after the pattern of
God, with power to think, reason, discern, love, worship, hope, plan, work out a plan, and know God.
God gave the first man a name, Adam, and then he named his wife and the other creatures. One theory of
"modern thought" is that the name Adam means man in general and not one specific man. This is false, and from
it follows a number of false theories. To produce man at all, one first man must be made. He could not come by
chance (as the evolution theory guesses). He had to be supernaturally made by One greater than himself. That
One is God. Adam was that first man.
What is God's purpose in making man a living soul and in the image of God? It is that man might show forth
God's g lor y and pra is e (Isaiah 43:7, 21). It is that He mig ht have a fr iend, a child, to br in g forth pleasure
to H im and to live with Him in love and fellows hip ( Revelatio n 4:11). It is trag ic that all men do not enter into
H is fellows hip. Ther e is good r eason. R e ad Isaiah 59:1-4.
Supernaturally Placed
Genesis 2:8-15 Man was perfect and good when created. God put the good man in a good place—a garden
eastward in Eden—a place specially prepared for man. There was everything man would need. There were
rivers, and there were trees for beauty and trees for food. In the midst of the garden, easily reached, were the
© 2015 Church of God, Inc.
Supernatural Origin─ Lesson 1
www.GodsAcres.org
SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 1
tree of life and the tree of knowledge of good and evil. None were either of man's planning or making. They
were gifts from God. They opened unlimited avenues of joy and happy achievement. Into this wonderful garden,
God put man to dress it and to keep it. There was only one restriction. Had man obeyed, how different his
history!
There were two special trees in the garden within reach of man. One was forbidden to him, one was not.
Man made a tragic choice to eat of the wrong one—chose death instead of life. By this he came short of the
glory of God. Because of this man had to be removed from reach of the tree of life. By their wrong choice
Adam and Eve set their feet in wrong paths and led their descendants there. They began to devise religions of
their own, none of which can free man from death. The one remedy lies in receiving Christ Who came that we
might have life (John 10:10).
Supernatural Law
Genesis 2:16-20 Of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat. This was the sum total
of that first supernatural law. This first law has been the basis of man's relationship with God constantly
throughout the Word of God from that day until now. A valid law carries a reward for obedience and a penalty
for disobedience. Here the reward would have been the smile of God, joy, harmony, and fellowship with Him.
The penalty—thou shalt surely die. Disobedience is sin. Sin always brings death (James 1:15). In the day that
thou eatest thereof . . . Did they die then? Yes, instantly (Chapter 3). Death is separation. Their sin separated
them from God. Instead of being spiritually alive, they were then spiritually dead. Everywhere we see the
working of death. Thank God for the Savior Jesus Christ Who has conquered death for every man (2 Timothy
1:10; Hebrews 2:14; 1 Corinthians 15:26). Take Him and have life (1 John 5:12).
Since all men were placed in this close connection with God, all are responsible as to how they maintain that
connection. Since souls come from God, they must be given back to Him again. The record of each life will be
laid bare at the judgment seat of Christ (Romans 14:10-12; Revelation 20:13). This is the supernatural
culmination of the religious system begun when God made man.
Supernatural Religion
There are many kinds of religion. Which one is right? To be effective, a religion must connect with greater
power than man has. To supply the needs of the human heart, a religion must come from a source outside of and
greater than that heart. It must be supernatural. It must come from God.
Many professed Christians think so lightly of God's authority over them. They think Him only remotely
concerned with their lives. They carelessly consider their relationship with God. They glance at Him and then
turn away to order their lives after their own thinking, to act in their own power. That is human religion. It is
natural rather than supernatural. It is false Christianity regardless of the name it claims.
We need to realize the immediate, continuous presence of God. We need to hold His majesty in awe. In our
memory verse God told Abram to walk before me, and be thou perfect. He pointed to His right to require this
of Abram—I am the Almighty God. He is also our Lord and Creator. He has the right to require perfect
obedience of us. We are each responsible to Him.
He will never accept a life lived separated from Himself. He paid the price of the life of Jesus Christ that we
might live in Him and He in us. Read Jesus' prayer in John 17:20-26. There is a difference between religion and
salvation. Salvation is the only religion that is supernatural.
JUST A THOUGHT
Your religion will do more for you if you do more for it,

LESSON 2
A SUPERNATURAL VOICE
Scripture Text: 1 Kings 18:1-39; 2 Corinthians 3:7-11
Looking at the lesson Scriptures, the readings and other recorded
events, we find that the experience of men under the Law was glorious.
God had contact with men and led them then. He answered prayers and
worked miracles. However, this glory came by the Law written in stone.
There was no power provided to obey. Sacrifice had to be made
continually for disobedience. The rule was "You shall." Now, "If you
love Me, you will."
That dispensation was supernatural, but this dispensation is more
glorious and supernatural. The supernatural runs throughout the history
of God's people. God talked to and worked with people in Old
Testament times. He continued to do so in New Testament times. His
dealing with men is more glorious in this Gospel dispensation than ever
before. In the Law dispensation, He was with His people, now He is in
them.
MEMORY VERSE: For if that which is done away was glorious, much more that which remaineth is
glorious.
—2 Corinthians 3:11
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—Genesis 18:16-33 The Lord talks to Abraham.
Tue.—Genesis 28:10-22 God speaks to Jacob.
Wed.—Exodus 11; 13:17-22 God led Moses and Israel.
Thu.—1 Samuel 30:1-19 David hears from God.
Fri.—Daniel 2 God reveals secrets to Daniel.
Devotional Reading: Acts 18:1-11 The Lord encourages Paul.
The Lord Speaks to Elijah
1 Kings 18:1-29 (For the whole story, read Chapters 17 and 18.) For the sins of Israel and of her king,
Ahab, God withheld rain for three years and six months. During the drought He supernaturally provided for His
prophet, Elijah. Then he instructed him to meet Ahab and arrange for a showdown on Mount Carmel before all
Israel to test whether Baal—a heathen god—or the Lord was the true God. The proof was to depend upon which
would send fire on a sacrifice. This was agreed, the prophets of Baal trying first. To their long and passionate
prayers, there was neither voice, nor any to answer, nor any that regarded. This is found in natural religion.
No positive results came from their efforts.
Elijah Simply Follows God's Plan
1 Kings 18:30-37 Elijah said unto all the people, Come near. Simply and plainly, he felt sure of success.
God had spoken, and he believed God. Before the thousands of Israel, he built up the broken altar of the Lord
and laid on it the wood and meat sacrifice. This was usual. Unusual was the trench dug around it and the twelve
barrels of precious water poured over it and filling the trench. Why? (1) There must be no question of trickery or
suspicion of fraud. (2) The event must be clearly seen to be a miracle—supernatural.
© 2015 Church of God, Inc.
A Supernatural Voice─ Lesson 2
www.GodsAcres.org
SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 2
God had spoken to Elijah, now Elijah speaks to God. He prayed simply and briefly. He acknowledged the
Lord as He Who had worked with Israel from its beginning. He asked Him to show the people (1) His power
and position and Lordship, (2) that Elijah was serving Him in doing this, (3) that God had directed in this, and
(4) that God was calling them back to Him.
God Answers
1 Kings 18:38-39 God was waiting for this moment. The fire of the Lord fell, and consumed the . . .
sacrifice . . . wood . . . stones . . . dust . . . water. Was this natural or supernatural? Could the people see that
there was a living God Who answered prayer and worked through men? Yes. The people knew. All doubts were
driven away. With a mighty shout, The Lord, he is the God; the Lord, he is the God; they fell on their faces
before Him.
When Israel was cleansed of the prophets of Baal, God sent rain. God's power had been shown.
The Greater Glory
2 Corinthians 3:7-11 If the ministration of death . . . was glorious . . . how shall not the ministration
of the spirit be rather glorious? The ministration of death was the Law dispensation exemplified by the Ten
Commandments written . . . in stones. It was of death because it had no power to take away the binding power
and guilt of sin. That dispensation is also the ministration of condemnation, because it condemned to just
punishment violators of rules, and that which is done away, because it lasted only until John the Baptist
preached Jesus Christ (Luke 16:16). Yet this system of death and condemnation was glorious in its time in
God's plan. Read of the marvelous manifestations of God at the giving of the Law (Exodus 19), the shining of
His glory in the face of Moses (Exodus 34:29-35), and the filling of His glory in the tabernacle at its completion
(Exodus 40:34-38). We find many other examples of the glorious character of the Law dispensation. But it had
no glory in this respect, its glory was overshadowed by reason of the glory that excelleth, or is greater. What
is this greater glory? The ministration of the spirit, the dispensation in which God moves into the heart of man,
transforming him and enabling him by His Spirit to keep the Law of God. This is the dispensation in which we
live, the age of the Gospel of Jesus Christ. It is the ministration of righteousness because it has the Savior
Who died to make men righteous. It is that which remaineth because it is permanent. This dispensation is to
last until Jesus comes at the end of the world. This is more glorious than the Law dispensation. Then God talked
to and worked with His people. Now He lives in them and works through them.
Can We Expect Supernatural Workings?
We can have prayer answers, miracles, guidance from God, hearts made new by divine power. Jesus Christ
is our contact with God. The people in Old Testament times who experienced the things of God were those who
surrendered to and obeyed Him. He works through human channels surrendered, free of sin, and filled with His
Spirit. This state is reached by putting faith in the Son of God Who loved us and gave Himself for us.
We must be believing, repenting, and surrendering so that He may live in us. This supernatural presence and
power must be active in us. We cannot live without it. We are crucified with Christ that He may live in us
(Galatians 2:20). Read the Words of Jesus in John 14:12, 14, 17, and 23. Surely this is supernatural presence
and power active in human lives.
JUST A THOUGHT
A man’s conscience, and not his mattress, has most to do with his sleep.

LESSON 3
A SUPERNATURAL COVENANT
Scripture Text: Galatians 3:6-18
God's basic program of relationship with man has never
changed. It is an everlasting covenant. He has used different
methods at times, but the everlasting covenant of faith runs
throughout. Salvation is by faith in God's promises and not by
feelings or man's own efforts.
One of the most common errors in religious thinking is to
trust in one's own good works to save him. Many try to be saved
by keeping a law. But the inheritance is not of the law but of
promise. Our believing shapes our doing. Some teach that
Christ's righteousness is imputed to a believer regardless of his
works. This is false. If faith is not enough to change one's
motives and produce good works, it is not faith. We see in James
2:20-24 that real God-given faith is imputed . . . for
righteousness because it produces righteousness. It opens the
heart into which Christ can pour His righteousness, making the
heart right. By this, man is made the righteousness of God in Christ (2 Corinthians 5:21). A saint has
imparted righteousness as well as imputed righteousness.
MEMORY VERSE: And I will establish my covenant between me and thee and thy seed after thee in their
generations for an everlasting covenant, to be a God unto thee, and to thy seed after thee.
—Genesis 17:7
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—Genesis 9:8-17 The rainbow covenant with Noah.
Tue.—Genesis 17:1-22 Everlasting covenant through Isaac.
Wed.—Psalm 105:1-15 God remembers His covenant.
Thu.—Exodus 24:1-8 The blood of the covenant.
Fri.—Romans 9:1-16 A covenant of faith and grace.
Devotional Reading: Isaiah 54:1-10 God's covenant of peace.
People of Faith Are the Children of Abraham
Galatians 3:6-9 Abraham believed God. Real faith is not as common as people would make it seem. To
believe is to trust and obey. Abraham did, and God accounted it righteousness. Belief is what God wants most.
Without belief, there cannot be obedience. Belief brings action. (See Romans 4:13-25.) They which are of
faith . . . are the children of Abraham. Believing God and His promises puts one in the family with others who
do so. When God told Abraham In thee shall all nations be blessed (Genesis 12:3), He referred to the gospel
of Jesus Christ to come many centuries later, by which the heathen (the unsaved) would be justified (saved)
through faith in Christ—the same way that Abraham received his blessings. This blessing is received in
Abraham because Jesus was humanly a descendant of Abraham.
The Law Cannot Justify
Galatians 3:10-14 The Law is of works, of what one must do or not do. One living under it is bound by its
penalties, its curse for disobedience. Since no one can keep it perfectly in his own strength, no soul can be made
© 2015 Church of God, Inc.
A Supernatural Covenant─ Lesson 3
www.GodsAcres.org
SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 3
alive or kept alive by it. How then? The just shall live (or be made alive) by faith (Habakkuk 2:4; Hebrews
10:38), by believing and obeying Christ. Jesus Christ redeems from the curse of the Law. The curse of the Law
is death, for the soul that sinneth, it shall die (Ezekiel 18:4). One choosing to live by the Law has only the
reward that the Law can give, but one living by the promise of God receives all that the promise includes.
Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law. How? By Himself becoming a curse for us by hanging
on a tree (cross)—being crucified (Deuteronomy 21:22-23). He died with the sins of all the world on Him, thus
as the worst sinner. The Holy God stooped this low for us so that we might have the blessing of Abraham . . .
through Jesus Christ. What was this blessing? The promise of the Spirit through faith. This is what God
planned when He made the covenant with Abraham (Genesis 12 and 17).
Works may be our own, done in our natural, human strength. Many unsaved people live orderly lives and do
good works. But faith connects one with God. That done by faith is done in the power of God. The Gospel is the
power of God, not the power of man. It is supernatural power (Romans 1:16). If living by faith does not bring
supernatural motives and works to our lives, it is not faith. Living by faith is a supernatural religion. When man
builds a religion, it is only a heathen religion, not the true religion of God. True religion was never evolved or
built by man. It came down from God. A supernatural religion MUST be a revealed religion.
The Covenant With Abraham Is Everlasting
Galatians 3:15-18 A covenant is binding. Even a man-made covenant is not to be changed or set aside. God
made this covenant with Abraham and his seed . . . which is Christ. He confirmed— ratified, established,
made sure—that covenant in Christ. That is, Christ was the confirmation, the fulfilling of it. It is by Christ's
sacrifice that we have the promise of the Spirit. The whole covenant of faith rests upon Christ. It is an
everlasting covenant—a supernatural covenant. (Psalm 105:8-10.)
Paul writes in Hebrews 13:20-21: Now the God of peace . . . through the blood of the everlasting
covenant (Christ's shed blood), Make you perfect in every good work to do his will, working in you that
which is well pleasing in his sight, through Jesus Christ.
The Law was given through Moses several hundred years after this covenant was made. It was added for a
time. It did not disannul, or set aside, the covenant of faith. The promise still stands. If the inheritance (the
promised gift of salvation and the filling with the Holy Spirit) be of the law, that is, if we earn it by doing things
the Law says, then it is no more of promise. But Abraham could not earn it by works. It was a gift God gave
him by promise. All receive God's salvation the same way—by promise, by grace—for it is an everlasting
covenant. Thank God for that! For who could ever earn it?
God's established relationship with man does not change. In the Father is no shadow of turning (James
1:17). Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and today, and forever (Hebrews 13:8). God has one permanent
covenant, one people, and one Spirit to live in them. The everlasting covenant reaches back to the beginning as
well as forward. By faith the worlds were framed. By faith Abel offered unto God . . . by which he obtained
witness that he was righteous . . . By faith Enoch was translated . . . By faith Noah . . . prepared an ark . . .
By faith Abraham . . . obeyed (Hebrews 11:3-8). That Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith (Ephesians
3:17). But without faith it is impossible to please him (Hebrews 11:6). What a marvelous gift Jesus offers us
when He says, "Come!"
JUST A THOUGHT
The only way to make the Gospel suit men
is to change men to suit the Gospel.

LESSON 4
A SUPERNATURAL SAVIOR
Scripture Texts: John 14:1-11; Luke 3:21-22; Luke 4:1, Luke 4:14
Jesus Christ was God in the flesh. He is the Son of God from Heaven. The Holy
Spirit filled Him. Only a supernatural One can save us. Only One Who is God can
give life.
Before we can have faith, we must have belief. The disciples already believed in
God; "believe also in me," Jesus said. It is comforting to have the assurance that in the church are many abiding
places. He spoke of preparing a place for them that they could have access to these abiding places. We have a
part in these also.
Jesus said, "And whither I go ye know, and the way ye know." Thomas answered, "Lord, we know not
whither thou goest; and how can we know the way?" The Lord answered, "I am the way." This was a reasonable
question. If the disciples did not know where Jesus was going, how could they follow Him? We often ask the
same questions today. Our Lord's answer to Thomas and to us is the same: Jesus Himself. When we accept Jesus
as the divine Son of God, then we find ourselves walking in the right pathway, the pathway of Truth.
MEMORY VERSE: For such an high priest became us, who is holy, harmless, undefiled, separate from
sinners, and made higher than the heavens.
—Hebrews 7:27
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—Isaiah 11:1-12 Jesus Christ foretold.
Tue.—Isaiah 61 The office of Christ foretold.
Wed.—Luke 4:16-24 Jesus claimed to fulfill Isaiah's words.
Thu.—John 7:14-46 Jesus came from the Father.
Fri.—Philippians 2:1-11 Jesus' name above every name.
Devotional Reading: Hebrews 7:14-28 Jesus is our High Priest.
The Great Claims of Jesus
John 14:1-6 Jesus stated to His disciples some of His reasons for leaving them. But they could not
understand. Thomas let this be known by his question. He asked Jesus how they could know the way to Him
when they did not know where He was going. Then Jesus made this supernatural statement, I am the way . . .
truth . . . life. All that man most wants and needs, Jesus is. The way to God and Heaven; the way to all good
living; the Truth among the many false theories of man; life itself, good and useful and happy and everlasting.
All these, Jesus IS. No one can have these without having Jesus. He is the only way to God, though many teach
otherwise. Only of One Who Himself is God could such claims be true. It takes supernatural power and
authority and life to be and do these things. Jesus said He had this power. He said He had power to both lay
down His life and take it up again. He said He could quicken the dead and give one eternal life. He said all
power in Heaven and Earth was given to Him. One making such a claim is either a liar or the Almighty God.
Jesus was no braggart. His works backed up His claims in manifestation of supernatural power.
Jesus' Connection With the Father
John 14:7-11 To know Christ is to know the Father. To see Christ is to see the Father. Christ is in the
Father, and the Father is in Him. Christ's Words and acts were done by the Father working through Him. By
these statements, Jesus testified of His deity. He came from God and is Himself God in the flesh, of the same

LESSON 4
substance as the Father. His claims are true. But if doubt dims the picture, look at His works—healings, raising
the dead, stilling the storm, and multiplying food. Let works which no other could do prove His deity. Yet the
Jews asked for signs after seeing His great works.
When Jesus said, He that hath seen me hath seen the Father . . . I am in the Father, and the Father in
me, did He mean They are one and the same Person? No. There is a teaching commonly known as "Jesus only
teaching." If Jesus was the only one, why did He speak at all of His Father? Why did He pray to Him? Why did
He say He was going to Him? God is three Persons—Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. How are They three and yet
in each other? Jesus is in His saints, yet both a saint and Christ each keep his separate, individual personality.
The Father living in and working through Jesus was supernatural power in Him.
Nothing Less Than Beloved Son Will Suffice
Luke 3:21-22 When Jesus was thirty years old, He was baptized in water by John the Baptist. His Father
answered by opening Heaven and in audible voice claimed Jesus as His beloved Son. This was no ordinary
happening. It was supernatural—all three Persons of God acting in a way to be manifest to the people. Jesus was
filled with the Holy Spirit from His birth. God only witnessed the presence of the Holy Spirit in Jesus by giving
Him bodily shape like a dove. He wanted the people to know that none of the three work separately, but always
in harmony together. John was convinced that Jesus is the Son of God (John 1:29-34).
One of the great songs of Zion begins, "Tempted and tried, I need a great Savior." This is the deep cry of the
heart of each of us. Where can we find this great Savior? Not in man, for all have sinned, and come short of
the glory of God (Romans 3:23). All men are lost and away from God, facing eternal damnation. All must be
cleansed and made alive. What can we do? Where can we go? Who can save? No striving, no education, no
scientific discovery can do it. No power on earth can do it. It must be a sinless, ever living, almighty,
supernatural, divine One. Jesus Christ is the only One, the only name under heaven given among men,
whereby we must be saved (Acts 4:12). If we do not believe in Him as the only supernatural Savior, we have
no other hope, but will die in our sins (John 8:24). Nothing less than being made a son of God will get one into
Heaven.
The Power of the Spirit
Luke 4:1 Jesus being full of the Holy Ghost . . . was led by the Spirit . . . The Holy Spirit led Jesus in His
work. Jesus yielded to Him and followed His leadership.
Luke 4:14 Jesus returned in the power of the Spirit . . . and there went out a fame . . . The power of the
Spirit joined with the power of the Son overcame all things. Supernatural power was so evident that people saw
and wondered and told it everywhere. This is the power that saved men from sin and death.
The Memory Verse speaks of Jesus our High Priest. He is chosen of God, is set apart to God, He offers gifts
to God, and has access to God to receive gifts and favors from Him. He represents man before God. He is holy,
harmless, undefiled, separate from sinners, and made higher than the heavens. What a High Priest! He
offered Himself as the greatest sacrifice to God. This is the One Who is our supernatural Savior. No other could
be.
JUST A THOUGHT
To remove the supernatural from Christianity
is to destroy Christianity itself.

LESSON 5
A SUPERNATURAL BOOK
Scripture Texts: Deuteronomy 30:11-16; John 6:63; Galatians
God has spoken to us His will. It is in the Bible. The Bible is a
God-given Book, not a man-written book. We are to believe and
obey it.
God gave the Bible. The Bible is God's Word, not man's. The
Bible is saturated with the Spirit of God and with His life-giving
Word. The Bible has power to lead us to God. These facts make the
Bible a supernatural Book, the only one in the world. Being supernatural, it is greater than a natural, human
book. For this reason it is not understood by the natural mind. To try to make the Bible understandable and
acceptable to the unsaved is to lower it to a lifeless book, helpless to lift man from his lost state. It takes the
Holy Spirit to open the living meaning of the Bible to us.
MEMORY VERSE: But he said, Yea rather, blessed are they that hear the word of God, and keep it.
—Luke 11:28
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—Deuteronomy 31:24-30 The Law kept in the ark.
Tue.—2 Kings 22 The Book of God found.
Wed.—Acts 13:38-52 Paul preaches the Word of God.
Thu.—James 1:19-27 Receive the engrafted Word.
Fri.—1 John 1:1-4; 1 John 2:1-6 To know Him, we must obey.
Devotional Reading: Deuteronomy 29:10-29 Punishment for forsaking God's Law.
God Has Made Known His Will
Deuteronomy 30:11-16 Moses was giving God's message to Israel in a final speech before his death. He
said God's commandment was not hidden from Israel. They need not go to Heaven or across the sea to find it.
God had brought it to them. It was in thy mouth—they knew and could repeat it—in thy heart—they
understood it. Their conscience told whether they were obeying or disobeying it. We have God's commandment
now even more fully than did Israel then (Hebrews 8:8-11). In this Gospel dispensation, we have the complete
Bible. Also, He has given the Holy Spirit to live in us to teach and guide (John 14:26; John 15:26; John
Man did not seek God to learn His will. God sought man. He said, I have set before thee this day life and
good, and death and evil. The choice is ours. To love the Lord thy God, to walk in his ways, and to keep his
commandments is the way to life and good. Any other way is sin—the way to death and evil. We find His
commandments in the Bible.
Christ's Words Are Spirit and Life
John 6:63 Jesus said The words that I speak unto you, they are Spirit, and they are life. The Spirit of
God both sent them and uses them. They are living and can give life. We find His Words in the Bible. The Spirit
of God is in the Bible, not in the paper and ink, but in the Word, the message. It was He Who dictated the Words
to holy men of God who wrote them down. The prophecy—the Word from God—came not . . . by the will of
man (2Peter 1:20-21). The Bible is not a man-made book. It is inspired by God.

LESSON 5
The Bible is to read and study and pray over and meditate on and know and love and live by. How can one
who does not know the Bible be guided by it? Jesus said, If my words abide in you . . . (John 15:7). We must
have His Words so deep in our hearts that they are part of us. How can the Holy Spirit open God's Word to us if
we do not expose ourselves to it and seek His enlightenment?
How can a home be Christian where God is not worshiped and His Word is not read? Children must be
taught that their greatest need is salvation through Jesus Christ, and their most necessary knowledge is of the
Bible. By leaving worship and Bible study to the church, a home is saying that these are not important in
personal life. In Matthew 28:19-20, Jesus gave a commission to every saved person to preach the Word. A
Scripture will reach hearts where our reasoning will not. It is God's means in our hands for taking the good news
of life in Christ to the world.
Paul Preached a Revealed Gospel
Galatians 1:11-12 Paul exhorted the Galatians to hold fast to the Gospel he had preached. Why? Because it
was a revealed Gospel. Because the Gospel is not after man—is not of man's making. Read 1 Corinthians 2:9-
14. Paul received it by the revelation of Jesus Christ. Christ first opened it to him on the Damascus Road, gave
him more in the house of Judas, and much more in Arabia (Acts 9:1-22; Galatians 1:15-17). We have that same
Gospel in the Bible. It is the revealed Word of God.
The Bible is the doctrine of the Church of God. It is not submitted to us for change or choice. Our part is to
hear and to keep (Memory Verse), to heed and to obey. The authority of God is in His Book. The same
authority is not in humanly-made creeds, doctrines, and rules. Men are not to add to it or take from it. Read
Deuteronomy 4:2; Proverbs 30:6; Revelation 22:18-19.
The Bible Is a Living Book
Hebrews 4:12 The word of God is quick—alive. It is powerful to enlighten, convince, convict of sin, and,
if obeyed, to transform lives. It is sharp, able to divide and separate between things so similar that human insight
can see no difference. It goes to the very center of Truth and opens it to us. It penetrates deep to discern
thoughts and intents of the heart. It uncovers motives either good or bad, and it points out guilt. It uncovers to
us the true condition of our hearts which we cannot see. We are not the Bible's judge, it is ours.
Man has heard from Heaven. God has given us the way by which we can live a happy life here and reach a
successful destination to life eternal. What if our Creator had left us to guess and stumble our way not knowing
where? But He is wise and loving. He gave man intelligence, personality, ability, and a desire to do well and
good. He communicated His will to man as His created beings. His message is brought to man in one Book that
above all others bears the mark of the supernatural. It is the Word of God—the Bible.
Thank God that He has revealed Himself to us in His Book and through His Son Jesus.
JUST A THOUGHT
A mirror shows our dirt but does not wash it off.
The Bible shows our sin, but only Christ can wash it away.

LESSON 6
A SUPERNATURAL CHURCH
Scripture Texts: Matthew 16:13-18; 1 Corinthians 3:9-11; Ephesians
The church is built by Jesus Christ on Christ as the Son of God. It is
made for God to live in. The Spirit of God in each binds the members to
Him and to each other.
We must believe by divine revelation to our hearts. Head belief is not
enough. Unless the Holy Spirit impresses in our hearts the Truth of Who
Jesus is, we cannot truly believe Him to be the Son of God and Lord of
all, cannot believe as we must to be saved (1 Corinthians 12:3). All
saved people believe that Jesus is the Christ because they experience Him
in their hearts. We must know Jesus personally, and Jesus must know us
for us to be saved and to be a part of the supernatural church.
MEMORY VERSE: And the Lord added to the church daily such as should be saved.
—Acts 2:47
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—Acts 2 The church established.
Tue.—Acts 3:1-16 The power of God in the church.
Wed.—Hebrews 9:1-14 Jesus' blood was shed to build the church.
Thu.—Hebrews 12:22-29 The divine character of the church.
Fri.—1 Peter 2:1-10 A spiritual house.
Devotional Reading: Colossians 1:12-23 Christ, Head of church.
A Supernatural Foundation
Matthew 16:13-18 Jesus asked His disciples, Whom do men say that I . . . am? The disciples, in response
to His question, expressed that men had various ideas as to Who He was. Then Jesus made it personal. But
whom say ye that I am? In answer to this question, Peter said, Thou art the Christ—the anointed One of
God—the Son of the living God. He saw and felt the supernatural in Jesus and so thought Him to be
supernatural. Yet his belief was not based on his human judgment. Neither did he take the word of other men.
Jesus said Blessed art thou, Simon Barjona: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my
Father . . . The Father in Heaven had revealed this Truth to Peter. And I say also unto thee, That thou art
Peter. Peter knew Jesus, and Jesus knew Peter. This is the true foundation of the church. Upon this rock I will
build my church. The church is not brick and mortar, it is people. Christ is the builder. He builds it on Himself.
It is on a solid, sure, unshakeable foundation, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it. No man, Peter
or any other could be this kind of foundation. The foundation of God standeth sure (2 Timothy 2:19).
Does it matter who built the church? The whole character of the church depends upon who built it. Only a
supernatural One can build a supernatural church. A man's church can give us only what a man has to give. Who
is the head of a man-made church? Who governs it? Is it Christ's body, the habitation of God, a church holy
and without blemish? Read Ephesians 5:27. Can man's church include all the saved and exclude all sinners?
Only Christ's building stands sure. Everything built by man will finally be swept away. Read Matthew 15:13
and Psalm 127:1.

LESSON 6
A Supernatural Building
1 Corinthians 3:9-11 Paul, writing to the church at Corinth, called them God's building. He and Apollos
had taught and suffered to get them built up in the faith. Yet he claimed no ownership or ruling authority over
them. They were but laborers together with God. The Church of God is God's. All Paul had done was by the
grace of God, the strength and life of God given him.
Paul had laid the foundation, started the local congregation and taught them the fundamentals of the
Gospel. Yet it was not his foundation, nothing he planned or made. One foundation has been laid, and no man
can lay another. The only foundation is Jesus Christ. Jesus laid Himself by dying and rising again to save
sinners and put them into the church, which he hath purchased with his own blood (Acts 20:28). Any group
not on this foundation is not the Church of God. Since there can be but one building on one foundation, there is
but one church. No man can build another.
A Supernatural Fellowship
Ephesians 2:19-20 When God delivers us from the power of darkness and translates us into the kingdom
of his dear Son (Colossians 1:13), He makes us fellow citizens with the saints. No one but the King can make
us citizens of the kingdom. He takes us into the household of God. No one but the Father of the family can take
us into the family. It is a supernatural process done by God. The saved one is united with Him and with others of
like relationship. No one becomes a member of the Church of God except by being born of God, not of the will
of man or by a man-made ceremony, but of God (John 1:13). Each citizen is built upon the foundation of the
church. As each one is saved, he is added—built upon Christ.
An Habitation of God
Ephesians 2:21-22 For what are we added? To be a holy temple . . . an habitation of God. God created us
for His pleasure, companionship, fellowship, and communion. He wants to live in us and work through us.
(Isaiah 43:21: Revelation 4:11.) This union is the closest possible—in the Lord . . . through the Spirit—the
joining in one of a human person and the Almighty God. He hath raised us up together, and made us sit
together in heavenly places in Christ Jesus (Ephesians 2:6). We are members of his body, of his flesh, and
of his bones (Ephesians 5:30). Our life is hid with Christ in God (Colossians 3:3). This is the position or
condition of the Church of God. Are you in it? Do not remain a stranger and foreigner. Come to Jesus.
Names Written in Heaven
Acts 2:47 The Lord added to the church. No one else can add members. Only the Lord knoweth them
that are his (2 Timothy 2:19). There is no need for man's membership rolls because God has the names written
in Heaven (Luke 10:20). Human rolls only confuse and deceive by a false standard of membership. There are
no sinners in the Church of God. He adds only the saved. All the saved are claimed by God. The church can
never be destroyed. It stands sure.
JUST A THOUGHT
You can preach a better sermon
with your life than with your lips.

LESSON 7
A SUPERNATURAL ENTERING IN
Scripture Texts: Ephesians 2:1-9; John 1:12-13; John 6:44; Mark 1:15
Natural man is dead in sin. By a supernatural work in the heart, God
makes the soul alive. Without this, no one can see the kingdom and
certainly not get into it. Our part is to repent and forsake sin and believe on
Christ.
In the lesson today we see that through the sacrifice of Jesus Christ,
the dividing wall between Jews and Gentiles has been broken down and
that all men of all nations and races are on level ground as regarding their
Christian privileges.
Paul, in writing to the church at Ephesus, tells of the great change
that comes in the life of a converted sinner who is now able to grasp God's
plan for man's life in this world. God's work of salvation sets forth for all
time a purpose showing the exceeding riches of His grace in kindness
toward us in Jesus Christ. God's plan for the ages is clearly seen in our Lord, Who prayed that they may all be
one.
MEMORY VERSE: No man can come to me, except the Father which hath sent me draw him: and I will
raise him up at the last day.
—John 6:44
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—John 3:1-17 Born of the Spirit.
Tue.—1 Peter 1:17-23 Not redeemed with corruptible things.
Wed.—1 John 5:10-18 Must have the Son to have life.
Thu.—2 Corinthians 5:14-21 Christ made sin for us.
Fri.—2 Corinthians 7:1-11 The result of repentance.
Devotional Reading: John 10:1-18 Christ is the Door.
Natural Man's Condition
Ephesians 2:1-3 And you hath he quickened—made alive —who were dead in . . . sins. Here are
described natural people who walked according to the desires of the flesh, the children of disobedience.
Among whom also we all had our conversation (conduct). ALL, every person is of this kind until saved. Dead
in trespasses and sins—sin always brings death to the soul. In Adam all die—he brought sin into the world,
and all partake of it (1 Corinthians 15:22; Romans 3:23). All give in to temptation, walk as the children of
wrath, follow the prince of the power of the air (Satan) obey the lusts of our flesh instead of God, and thus
reap corruption (Galatians 6:8). Flesh and mind are masters, and such people are natural, do not belong to
Christ, are not of His kingdom, for they that are Christ's have crucified the flesh with the affections and
lusts (Galatians 5:24). Such are under God's wrath. With God, sin is not placed in categories. Any sin, whether
it is considered large or small, places us under God's wrath. The natural (however good) leaves us dead souls.
Quickened and Raised by Grace
Ephesians 2:4-9 Here is a complete turnaround in description because these Ephesians had had a rightabout
change—change of masters, from the kingdom of Satan to the Kingdom of God, from death to life, from the

LESSON 7
world to the church. They had been dead in sins, but were now quickened. All saints are quickened together
with Christ and raised to heavenly places in Christ Jesus. How blessed—with Christ . . . in Christ. God hath
(present tense) quickened and raised up. This is now. That in the ages to come he might show the exceeding
riches of his grace . . . through Christ Jesus—greater blessings were to come.
The operation of quickening, saving the soul from sin and making it alive is by grace. It is the work of God,
His life given us by faith according to the everlasting covenant. (Lesson 3.) Not of yourselves . . . Not of works,
nothing any human can do in himself, not a reward for good deeds, impossible to be earned. Our works are
natural, earthly. Faith reaches the supernatural grace of God.
Must Be Born of God
John 1:12-13 This work in the heart makes us sons of God; it is being born . . . of God. It is not done of
the will of man —is nothing man can do. Our part is to believe on his name. When we believe, we receive.
This is a supernatural work by God's grace. In John 14:6 we read, Jesus saith . . . no man cometh unto the
Father, but by me. To reach God and Heaven, we must receive Jesus Christ, must have Him living within us.
Christ in you, the hope of glory (Colossians 1:27).
What are some ways believed to be acceptable for entrance into the Kingdom of God and Heaven? "If I keep
the Ten Commandments—live by the Golden Rule—do the best I can— have been baptized in water—have
joined some church." There are a number of others, all of which are substitutes, additions, and are all futile and
wrong. They may give a sense of false security, causing many to think they are accepted by God when no work
has been wrought in the heart.
The Father Must Draw Us
John 6:44 . . . except the Father which hath sent me draw him. The Trinity always works in cooperation,
together. The Spirit convicts (John 16:8), the Father draws, the sinner yields, and Jesus enters the heart. It is a
time of refreshing that comes from the presence of the Lord (Acts 3:19). It is a supernatural process.
Our Part in Salvation
Mark 1:15 As Jesus began His work on earth, He preached, repent ye, and believe the gospel. Why? To
enter the kingdom of God He was setting up. Christ died for all, but not all accept life from Him. Not all enter
the kingdom. Except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish . . . he that believeth not shall be damned (Luke
13:3; Mark 16:16). Repentance and faith in Jesus Christ opens the way for God to work. Then by His power,
we are born again and taken into the kingdom. Even faith and repentance are gifts of God (2 Timothy 2:25;
Romans 12:3). We must listen and obey His drawing.
JUST A THOUGHT
A religion that will not take you to church services
will not take you to Heaven.

LESSON 8
A SUPERNATURAL INDWELLLING
Scripture Text: John 14:16-27
Not only does God do a work in the heart, making it alive and holy
and taking one into the church, but He also comes into the person to live
and work. When He comes in, He bears witness, letting the person know
he is a child of God (Romans 8:16). There is fellowship with God as
well as with His saints. There is an interflow of communion and prayer.
There is a power over sin and power in witnessing of Christ. There is
love, the love of God shed abroad in the heart by the Holy Ghost.
In five chapters of John are recorded the most intimate conversation
and communion of Christ with His twelve disciples. Our lesson is part of
that sacred talk.
MEMORY VERSE: Ye are of God, little children, and have overcome
them: because greater is he that is in you, than he that is in the world.
—1 John 4:4
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—Ephesians 1:3-19 Wisdom and knowledge of Spirit.
Tue.—John 16:1-15 The coming of the Spirit.
Wed.—Acts 4:1-33 The Spirit working.
Thu.—1 John 4:1-11 True or false spirits.
Fri.—1 Corinthians 2 True wisdom is the gift of God.
Devotional Reading: John 17:6-26 Church one with Father, Son.
The Comforter in Us
John 14:16-17 When Jesus was about to die, He gathered His twelve disciples in an upper room to
strengthen them for the experiences that would try their faith in coming days. He gave a most precious promise.
I will pray the Father—Jesus never worked independently. The Father would send another Comforter, the
Spirit of truth. His coming was not to be temporary but to abide with you forever. Some cannot receive Him.
The world cannot because they are separated from Him by their sin. Yet He is promised to every person who
meets the conditions for receiving Him (Acts 2:38-39). The Holy Spirit cannot come into sinful hearts. First, we
must be cleansed by faith in the shed blood of Jesus Christ as the atonement for sin. The disciples had done this.
They knew the Spirit—he dwelleth with you. But a greater blessing was to come. He shall be in you. First,
with, then, in. On the Day of Pentecost, He came in (Acts 2).
Christ in Us
John 14:18-21 Jesus was to leave the earth, but would still be in contact with His people. He would come to
them, they would see Him, His life would be theirs, they would be in Him and He in them, He would love them
and they, Him, and He would make Himself known to them. Because I live—He spoke of a supernatural
resurrection and life forevermore. Ye shall live also. His eternal life He gives to His people.
To whom does God give eternal life? To those who keep His commandments. Not just the Ten
Commandments. Love is shown by obedience to every Word of God (Luke 4:4). The disobedient do not love
Him. The teaching that one can sin and remain a child of God is false.

LESSON 8
How does one know Jesus is in him and in the Father? How does he know the Bible is true? That Jesus lives
and saves sinners? Not only because he reads it in the Bible, but he feels and experiences these. His presence in
him gives him proof that is greater than any head belief. It is supernatural knowledge. He feels the supernatural
life within him.
The Father in Us
John 14:22-24 The disciples did not understand. If Jesus came physically, would He not be visible to all?
Jesus answered . . . If a man love me, he will keep my words: and my Father will love him, and we will . . .
make our abode with him. Jesus explained that by love and obedience, both He and the Father are brought to
abide spiritually in one's heart. They come in the person of the Holy Spirit. Obedient ones see and hear and
know God spiritually. Love flows between them. Spiritual things are closed to those who do not love and obey
God's Word. They are blind to things of God. They do not know Him. He is not in them.
We must be indwelt to live a full Christian life. For instance, we can expect a cow to fly as much as we can
expect an unsaved one to love his enemies. He must first be indwelt by God Who is love. Do not ask, "Is my
work great, influential, known, and honored?" But, "Is God in it?" A saved man is a changed man. All things
are become new (2 Corinthians 5:17). A saved man is one with supernatural life—eternal life—and power
because he is possessed by a supernatural Person. Living water must first flow in before it can flow out. The
Spirit of God is that living water (John 7:38; John 4:14).
How to Be Indwelt
Jesus said, If a man love me, he will keep my words: and . . . we will make our abode with him . . . The
Father . . . shall give you another Comforter. The disciples had to wait several days for this Comforter. We do
not need to wait, He is here with us now. Romans 5:1-2 says, we are justified by faith, and also we have
access by faith into this grace wherein we stand. First, we must be saved from sin; then, the Spirit of God
comes in and gives us the power to stay saved. His indwelling gives one power to keep from committing sin
every day (Titus 2:11-12). From these and other Scriptures, we conclude that one is filled with the Holy Spirit
by first being justified or saved from sin, then by faith opening the heart to receive Him. It cannot be a
halfhearted invitation, but a full and complete consecration of all one is and has to His control. It is death to self,
crucifying the old man of the flesh (Romans 6:1-6). Surrender unconditionally and completely to God to do His
will in your life.
Holy Spirit Teaches Spiritual Things
John 14:25-27 Jesus was then present physically, in body. They saw Him with their physical eyes. After His
departure, the Holy Spirit would come not as a body but as a Spirit. He would live in their bodies. He shall
teach you . . . bring all things to your remembrance—give you understanding of spiritual things. Then these
strange sayings of Christ would be clear to them. (See 1 Corinthians 2:11-14.) Spiritual things cannot be
understood except by the Spirit of God. My peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth . . . The world can
give material, perishable, outward things. Only God can give eternal things, spiritual things, inward things,
which bring peace to the soul. He gives us Himself and with Him comes all that He has (Romans 8:32).
JUST A THOUGHT
It is a bit difficult to sell anyone a product
you have never used or a religion you have never lived.

LESSON 9
DIFFERENT SUPERNATURAL GIFTS
Scripture Texts: 1 Corinthians 12:4-11, 1 Corinthians12: 27-
31; Ephesians 4:8-13; 1 Peter 4:10-11
God's plan for accomplishing the work of the church is by
gifts of the Holy Spirit. These are abilities given to Spirit-filled
people.
Jesus left a commission for His church to carry out
(Matthew 28:19-20). He sent the Holy Spirit to endue with
power from on high to carry it out (Luke 24:49). We cannot
do it without the skills He gives. He must give the gift and the
power within us to use it. Look at each gift. How necessary is it
to the work of converting sinners or nurturing saints?
MEMORY VERSE: But the manifestation of the Spirit is
given to every man to profit withal.
—1 Corinthians 12:7
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—1 Corinthians 14:1-20 Place of gift of tongues.
Tue.—1 Corinthians 14:21-40 Orderly direction of the gift.
Wed.—Ephesians 4:1-16 Gifts and their purpose.
Thu.—Acts 19:1-20 Paul using gifts of the Spirit.
Fri.—2 Timothy 1:1-11 Our gift needs stirring up.
Devotional Reading: Romans 12:1-9 Using the gifts.
Different Gifts, but Same Spirit
1 Corinthians 12:4-6 By observing the church, we will agree that different people have different gifts and
talents. Yet the same divine qualities of love and Truth are common to all. One Spirit gave them. One Lord over
all binds into the body of Christ, one church. (See verses 12-13.) The gifts are abilities, not natural ones, but
specially given ones, supernatural ones. Differing gifts supply all the functions necessary to the perfect working
of the church. One Spirit being the source of them assures harmony. The church is compared to the human
body— one body, but many parts performing different duties.
God did not plan His church to stumble along as hit-and-miss, unskilled laborers. Yet we must admit that
much of it is doing just that. Where are the gifts? Are we aware of them? Do we seek them and expect to receive
them? Are we working as of the ability which God giveth? Does each know what is his gift, his skill from
God, his special place of service? Are we as individual members capable of leading a sinner to Christ? Can you
imagine workers going to their place of employment not knowing what their work is? In the church, everyone
has a place. But now hath God set the members every one of them in the body . . . (verse 18). This is God's
plan. Yet there is so little seeking for spiritual gifts. In verse 31 Paul wrote, But covet earnestly the best
gifts—not best in earthly gain or praise, but best in the glory they bring to God. Seek Him in prayer, consecrate
fully to Him, greatly desire gifts, ask for the gifts He wants you to have. Ask His help in using them.
Gifts Given to Profit All
1 Corinthians 12:7-11 The gifts are a manifestation of the Spirit. He does the works using the person as a
tool, yet not without or against the person's will in the matter. The spirits of the prophets are subject to the

prophets (1 Corinthians 14:32). We can refuse to let Him use us as He wishes, but this would be turning from
Him to sin.
Each gift is given to profit withal—(1) to bring spiritual growth to the person and to the rest of the church,
(2) to bring sinners to the Lord, (3) to bring glory to God. Some gifts are named here. Knowledge is a store of
facts and understanding of meanings. Wisdom is ability to use knowledge to lead to the best results. Discerning
of spirits is the ability to know what spirit is controlling a person or situation. Prophecy is the receiving of a
message from God and passing it on to others. Tongues are languages. The gift enables one to speak a tongue he
has not learned.
Read in Acts how the church was governed by the Holy Spirit through the gifts. Where there is usurping of
the Spirit's place, troubles arise. Men try to run things in their human strength. They elect or appoint people to
the various positions. They make rules and form doctrines. They plan and execute those plans. All according to
their own best judgment. God knew the problems of the church would come from within and provided for all the
problems the church would meet.
Specific Gifts
1 Corinthians 12:27-31 Exercise of the gift one has makes him a skilled workman in that line. An apostle,
for instance, is not made by electing a man one. He is made one by receiving gifts from the Holy Spirit and
using them in the work of an apostle—planting the Gospel in new places. It is the same with all the gifts. By
means of gifts, God sets people in their places in the church (verse 18), some apostles . . . prophets . . .
teachers . . . workers of miracles . . . healings, helps, governments . . . tongues. It is a supernatural operation,
not a human arrangement.
Purpose of the Gifts
Ephesians 4:8-13 When Jesus left the earth, He sent back spiritual gifts to men. Then He gave the gifted
men as gifts to mankind. They were apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors, and teachers. What are they for? (1)
For the perfecting of the saints—to aid the spiritual growth of every saved one from conversion to maturity in
Christ. (2) For the work of the ministry—all the work of the church, not preaching only. (3) For the edifying
of the body of Christ (the church), their uplift, culture, education in things of God, spiritual development. Their
goal is to make the church like Christ, perfect in holiness, to bring the unity of the faith . . . unto a perfect
man . . . of the fullness of Christ.
Using the Gifts
1 Peter 4:10-11 The use of our gifts is not optional with us. God does not give us a choice. The gifts are of
the grace of God, given from His very life. We are but stewards of them. They must bring honor to God.
Whatever we do in speaking or serving in any way, we must do it as of the ability which God giveth. That is,
we must let God work through us by means of our spiritual gift and not depend upon our own natural human
ability.
God not only fits a man for the work, He fits the work to the man. God does not force into unwilling
servitude. He makes us laborers together with God (1 Corinthians 3:9). He takes us into His confidence, calls
us not servants but friends (John 15:15). With His gifts comes a desire to use them. In using them is a fullness
of living joy unknown to one who is a mere member in a human organization. The gifts and their use are
supernatural.

LESSON 10
A SUPERNATURAL WALK
Scripture Texts: 2 Corinthians 5:17-18; 1 Peter 2:2-3; 1 John 3:9; Galatians
Yielding to Jesus is the basic requirement of the Gospel. Such yielding does
not patch up a life or merely improve it; it makes a life over. The old things—lust,
jealousy, selfish impulses, doubts, anger, and all things detrimental to living a
holy life—pass away when one walks with Jesus.
When a man is in Christ, his life becomes radiant, helpful, pure, and his
thoughts and acts become transformed with a new and beautiful Spirit. The
redeemed man is not taken out of this world, but the world is taken out of him.
Instead, he remains in the center of daily activity, and the purposes and
opportunities once spent in the interests of sin are now spent to the glory of God.
The daily walk of a child of God is directed and empowered by God. It is a
walk made new by Christ, a walk with supernatural spiritual food, supernatural
power, and supernatural results.
MEMORY VERSE: For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God.
—Romans 8:14
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—Ephesians 6:1-18 Fighting God's warfare in His power.
Tue.—Romans 8:6-14 Walking in the flesh or in the Spirit.
Wed.—Colossians 2:6-15 Continuing in Christ.
Thu.—2 Peter 1:1-11 Spiritual growth of a saint.
Fri.—Acts 9:10-20 Ananias obeys the Lord.
Devotional Reading: John 15:1-10 Can do nothing without Christ.
A New Creature
2 Corinthians 5:17-18 Therefore if any man be in Christ . . . Therefore always refers back to previous
verses—he is a new creature. A saved person is a changed one, made new, one renewed to such an extent that
he becomes an absolutely new being. Jesus Christ does not just improve a man or patch him up, He makes him
over. Sin is gone from the heart. The flesh is no longer master, Jesus is. Now all things are of God. The
supernatural God has taken over the life: actions (our walk) are directed by God. Upon conversion, many things
are cast out of one's life forever, but there are many things which are kept in one's life and transformed into
usefulness to God's work.
A Walk by the Word and of Prayer
1 Peter 2:2-3 As a newborn baby needs physical food, so a soul needs spiritual food. Food for the soul is
received from two sources: (1) From Bible study. God's Word is taken into the mind, goes into the heart, and is
transformed into thoughts, motives, and acts. (2) By daily communion with God through prayer. The life of a
saint is a walk of obedience to God. He has tasted of the graciousness of the Lord. Jesus promised answers to
prayer (Matthew 6:6). A saint goes to God for daily directions, for nourishment, fellowship, courage, and
strength.

A Walk of Holiness
1 John 3:9 Those born of God do not commit sin. They have holy—sin-free—lives (Hebrews 12:14).
Why? The seed of God is in them, the life of God. He cannot sin. God cannot sin, and He gives one the desire
not to sin and the power to carry out his desire. A sinning child of God is an impossibility. Daily conduct is
where either the natural or the supernatural shows at work in the life. Holiness is where the inner springs of the
life bubble forth and reveal whether they be of God or not.
In 2 Corinthians 4:7 we read, We have this treasure in earthen vessels. We are made of dust, are weak,
only human. We have no power for living or giving out the Gospel. The Excellency of the power MUST be of
God, not us. It is an asset to our walk with God if we will praise Him as we see the Gospel shown forth in our
lives.
Bearing Fruit of the Spirit
Galatians 5:22-23 Where the Holy Spirit lives, He bears fruit. These are inward virtues which produce
outward acts. A child of God walks differently from natural people of the world. The supernatural grace of God
in his life teaches him to deny ungodliness and worldly lusts and to live soberly, righteously, and godly, in
this present world (Titus 2:11-12). When one is born of the Spirit, he bears the fruit of the Spirit. As he yields
continually to the Spirit's control, he bears more and more fruit.
The Christian life is not a hard, restricted way, forced into a mold it does not fit. Christ's yoke is easy and
His commandments are not grievous. Salvation is not a burdensome effort to do right. Rather, it is the power to
do right. In 1 John 4:7-8 we read, love is of God. Here is the reason why the Christian walk is fitting for him.
The Christian walk is a walk of love. This is not a human love, but the same love God has. Without this
supernatural love, we are only natural man—unsaved. He that loveth not knoweth not God. How can we get
this divine love? To have corn, we must have corn seed. To have love, we must have Him Who is love. The love
of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost (Romans 5:5).
But this life is not without temptation. Satan is ever scheming to catch us unawares. We are still in the world
where all meet hardship, pain, sorrow, and disappointment. But none need go back into sin if he will watch and
pray diligently with faith and trust in God. If, in a careless moment, he is overcome by Satan, he should
immediately repent and seek forgiveness (1 John 2:1). Unregenerate people love their family and friends with
human love. God requires love that comes from Him.
Form the Good Habits
Since prayer and God's Word are so essential to Christian growth, every home should practice daily family
worship—prayer and Bible reading with the whole family together. Each one immediately upon being saved
should set aside time each day for private Bible study and prayer besides the family worship. This will prove to
be one of the greatest sources of growth in grace and of strength against temptation and backsliding. Sons of
God are led by the Spirit. Led signifies not a once-for-all experience, over and done, but a continuous day-by-
day walk with God. It is growth in grace. It is the path of the just (Proverbs 4:18).
JUST A THOUGHT
Some people send up a ten-cent prayer
and expect a million-dollar answer.

LESSON 11
A SUPERNATURAL WARFARE
Scripture Texts: Ephesians 6:10-20; Romans 14:19-21
The Christian battle is not against men but against the sins and mistaken
notions of men. Evil men in the world are but the victims of perverted
ideas—the agents, either intentionally or unintentionally, of a vast empire
controlled by Satan which plagues human life. The Bible very plainly teaches
that angels have their adversaries in demons, and God has an arch enemy
opposing His righteous purpose, namely Satan.
We must remember that our weapons are spiritual arms. We cannot fight
temptations with swords of steel. The Sword of the Spirit is the Word of God,
it is not our sword. It alone is sufficient for the saint's victory.
What an excellent figure of speech Paul employed in describing the
Christian soldier. To him, every piece of the soldier's equipment
corresponded to some spiritual power of which Paul knew by experience.
MEMORY VERSE: Put on the whole armor of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.
—Ephesians 6:11
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—Proverbs 4:10-19 Contrast of the wise and wicked.
Tue.—1 Thessalonians 5:12-22 A practical Christian climate.
Wed.—1 John 2:18-29 Hold to true doctrine.
Thu.—Romans 8:26-39 Persecution not separate from Christ.
Fri.—1 Peter 1:13-25 Gird up the loins of your mind.
Devotional Reading: 1 Corinthians 9:15-27 Rights surrendered.
Our Enemy Forces Are Unseen
Ephesians 6:10-12 Finally . . . be strong in the Lord . . . Be empowered by the Spirit of the living God, be
made powerful in the strength of His might—the supernatural power and strength. How? By putting on the
whole armor of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil. One of the ways the Bible
uses to describe life is that life is a pilgrimage, and also that it is a battlefield. There is much teaching and a lot
of worldly literature today which reflects the idea that life is a carefree adventure. We know this is not true.
Christians are the happiest people in the world, but they are happy pilgrims, happy warriors. Every religious
person puts on some of the armor of God. But the true Christian puts on the whole armor of God as we are
admonished in God's Word. To him, this is a way of life. Its doctrines are very important. So is the type of
conduct which grows out of these doctrines. We wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against . . . spiritual
wickedness . . . We fight an unseen enemy.
On our Mounts of Transfiguration, amid circumstances where we expect to find only God and His
righteousness—in the heavenly places—we often encounter the spiritual host of wickedness.
The Christian's Equipment
Ephesians 6:13-17 We are wise to remember that all human problems are basically spiritual problems.
Again, the Apostle emphasizes the necessity for taking the WHOLE armor of God. Do not take some of the
Bible and cast the rest aside. Do not rush to God in an eager desire to be helpful along certain lines and then rush
