to the world and its pleasures seeking satisfaction at other times. The Christian's equipment is: (1) THE
GIRDLE—A wide belt which was central in the whole attire of the soldier. Likewise, a strong conviction of
Truth is central in the life of every valiant soldier of Christ. (2) THE BREASTPLATE—A protection of the
soldier's vital organs. The saint must have a reputation and record of righteousness as a breastplate. The more
we are known to be on the right side of the fence morally, the less will evil people seek us out and try to tempt
us. (3) SHOES—Roman soldiers wore sandals bound by firm thongs, and the soles were studded with nails. Let
the Gospel be to you, says Paul, what the firm sandal is to the Roman soldier.
Your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel . . . The word preparation is the translation of a Greek
word which means establishment, or firm foundation. Have a hold on the Gospel which will really be to you a
firm foundation. (4) THE SHIELD OF FAITH—By faith, the enemy is shut out from all directions in the battle.
The shield of faith puts the enemy to flight. It opens the way for the supernatural strength of God to take us
through. (5) HELMET OF SALVATION—Let your salvation be like a helmet on your head. There will be times
when you will not feel that you are saved. But remember that one is not saved by feelings, but by faith, believing
that Christ died for your sins as His part, and that your salvation was gained when you accepted Christ as
your Savior. Go before the throne of grace in the name of Him Who sealed the covenant by His blood. Go
before Him day-by-day, cast yourself upon Him for support and power. By obedience, we can be saved even if
we do not feel it. Sin alone can separate one from God. (6) THE SWORD OF THE SPIRIT—Remember that
your arms are spiritual arms. We cannot fight temptations and unseen enemies with swords of steel. The Word
of God is the Spirit's sword, not ours. It alone is sufficient for the saint's victory in this great battle of spiritual
life or death.
Our Power Is in Prayer
Ephesians 6:18-20 Paul now changes the setting from soldier to saint, from battlefield to prayer chamber.
As the natural army needs a supply line as a source of supply for its needs, so the soldier of Christ needs a
supply line for all his needs. Praying . . . in the Spirit, and watching . . . with all perseverance . . . lest the
wiles of the devil overwhelm you. Paul makes plain what Christ before him had made plain, namely, that there
is no spiritual power without prayer. Prayer is the difference between our house being built upon the sand or
upon the rock. Paul also tells us that our prayers will help others as well as ourselves. Supernatural prayer brings
supernatural victory. Sometimes we are unable to help a person in any other way, but we can always pray for
them. We tap resources of spiritual power which will be available to them and to us in the achieving of victory.
Our Lord was a man of prayer; He needed prayer, and so do we.
The Secret of Survival
Romans 14:19-21 Let us . . . follow after the things which make for peace. Things which lift up our
brother not put him down. Climate is an important factor for the farmer and the growing of crops. Climate is
also important to those who would have their lives bring glory to God. The place for a saint is with the saints.
The atmosphere he should seek is the atmosphere which will be conducive to his soul's growth. If you would
fight a successful fight, do not warm yourself by the enemy's fire. Do not associate with the agnostics, the
scoffers, and the other enemies of Christ.
Paul goes on to make us aware that we are our brother's keeper. The welfare of men's souls is the most
important issue he maintained. The early church was largely made up of Jews who had been converted to
Christianity. These people still had deep convictions about clean and unclean foods. On the other hand, Gentiles
in the church had no convictions about these things, and there was contention between them about these things.
Paul said to stop contending with each other about clean and unclean food. If something you are eating or doing
is causing your brother to be weakened spiritually, Paul instructs you to abstain from that. Leave it to your
pastor to straighten out their problems.

LESSON 12
A COUNTERFEIT OF THE SUPERNATURAL
Scripture Texts: Revelation 18:1-5; Galatians 1:8-12; Matthew 15:13
About seven hundred years before the time of this prophecy, the
kingdom of Babylon conquered Judah and took the people into captivity
for seventy years (Jeremiah 52). Because of this, Babylon came to mean
captivity, forced servitude, foreign authority, and punishment for sin. At
the same site many years before, the Tower of Babel had been built
(Genesis 11:1-9). Here God had brought confusion of language which
stopped the work and dispersed the workers. From this event, Babel came
to stand for confusion, scattering, and failure because of pride, human
plans, and independence of God. The significance of all of these is
combined in the meaning of the word Babylon. It is a fitting description
for this religious evil. It is a counterfeit.
MEMORY VERSE: But he answered and said, Every plant, which my heavenly Father hath not planted,
shall be rooted up.
—Matthew 15:13
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—1 Kings 12:25-33; 1 Kings 13:1-10 Human worship punished.
Tue.—Ephesians 1:1-10 Chosen in Christ.
Wed.—Acts 19:11-20 False workers.
Thu.—1 John 4:13-21 Dwelling in God.
Fri.—2 Thessalonians 2:1-12 A falling away.
Devotional Reading: Matthew 15:1-14 Human religion wrong.
Babylon the Great
Revelation 18:1-3 Babylon the great is fallen. For something to fall, it had to be lifted to a higher plain
before. This great organization is fallen, not will fall. What has it fallen from? From Truth, righteousness, and
holiness. It is shown to be evil by the descriptive words—devils . . . every foul spirit, unclean and hateful bird
. . . fornication. It is widespread in its influence—all nations have drunk . . . kings . . . merchants of the
earth. It has controlled people, governments, and commerce, compelling to worship as it dictates. But now the
angel announces its downfall. What is it? The system of Catholicism is characterized as part of Babylon . . .
that great city, the beast. Catholicism, the beast, and Protestantism with all false religion is characterized as
Babylon. Protestantism is characterized as the image of the beast and the harlot daughters of the woman. It
includes all that partake of their nature—their spirit. The one principle running throughout all, and that which
makes it evil, is human rule. In the Church of God, Christ is the Head. In earthly religious organizations, man
assumes Christ's place of authority.
A Call to Separate
Revelation 18:4-5 Another voice from heaven . . . This was Christ Himself calling to the scattered
members of His body. Come out of her, my people . . . This is Christ's message to all the saved from sin in our
day. To remain in her (spiritual Babylon) gives support to her and approval to her sins. Remaining makes them
liable to her punishments. Christ's call is only to HIS PEOPLE—those honest-hearted ones who are truly saved,

LESSON 12
even though entangled in the evil system through ignorance. It is wrong for men to attempt to build a church, to
form a religious doctrine, or to rule the people of God. The chief wrong in these is substituting human rule for
divine rule. All such is doomed to destruction. A list of the terrible penalties for Babylon is recorded in verses
21-24 of this chapter. Her sins have reached unto heaven. There the record will be opened at the Judgment.
No Other Gospel
Galatians 1:8-12 There is no other gospel, no other true doctrine, than that which Paul preached, which is
the Gospel found in the New Testament. Why is it the only one? Because it is not after man. It was not Paul
who was persuading men, that is, not in his own ability or his authority. God was doing it through him. The
Gospel Paul preached was not man-made. Paul was not told it by man or educated into it. It is by the revelation
of Jesus Christ. Jesus revealed it to him. There is but one revealed and supernatural Gospel from God. This
Gospel ONLY can be rightfully passed on—unchanged, with no additions or subtractions. This is so important
that a curse is pronounced against any who teach or preach another (Revelation 22:19).
Strange Plants to Be Rooted Up
Matthew 15:13 Jesus was condemning the Pharisees' traditions and commandments of men. Then, Every
plant, which my heavenly Father hath not planted—every doctrine, rule, theory, creed, system, or
organization not from God—shall be rooted up. What then will be the fate of those entangled in the humanly
planted plants?
The difference is also in the authority behind the church. The Church of God has the authority of God.
Human organizations depend upon the authority of men. The church takes the authority of God's Word, the
Bible. Human organizations take that of their leaders, councils, conferences, creeds, disciplines, doctrines,
traditions, etc. They may say, "Christ is our Head." Why, then, have a man as head? Anything with two heads is
a freak, a monstrosity. What man has the right to take in or put out members, to write creeds, to negotiate
doctrines, changes, and mergers?
Counterfeit
A counterfeit dollar bill may look real, but it was not made by the government. A counterfeit church is any
not authorized by Christ and which places human authority where divine ought to be. Since one enters the
Church of God by spiritual birth, any group one can enter by joining can only be a counterfeit.
One may say, "I know people who belong to a certain denomination who are just as godly and filled with the
Spirit as anyone can be." Certainly. They look to God and His Word as their authority. They open their hearts to
Him. They belong to Him. These are the ones to whom Christ calls, Come out of her, my people, and stand in
Me alone. God desires His people to come out of her, and to stay out.
In these days, we are hearing much about an ecumenical movement which is attempting to build a one-world
church by uniting all denominations regardless of their belief. It includes the Word keepers, and they are blind to
the fact that Christ has already built a one-world church. It is the body of Christ. (Read Colossians 1:18, 24.)
There will never be another. There will never be a need for one, for the Church of God will never be destroyed.
(See Matthew 16:18.) Any other can be only a counterfeit. A humanly built church is a human church that is all.
It is only a religious organization—natural, not supernatural. Such will have union but will lack unity. No
mechanical union can produce spiritual unity. The difference is in the life which empowers the church. The
Church of God is the household of God, and her members are fellowcitizens . . . God keeps her membership
(Ephesians 2:19-22; 2 Timothy 2:19). They depart from iniquity—live holy.

LESSON 13
A SUPERNATURAL RESURRECTION
Scripture Texts: John 6:38-40; 1 Corinthians 15:19-23, 1 Corinthians
15:35-38, 1 Corinthians 15:42-56; 1 Thessalonians 4:13-18.
We have been studying of the good things Jesus prepared in this world
for His people. Today we look at some of the things He has prepared for
His people in the next world. They are all supernatural. After a person has finished a saved life here in this
world, what then? Jesus promised that He was going to the Father, to Heaven, where He had been in the
beginning. He said He was going back to the Father, and that each saint could go also. He prayed that those
given Him would be with Him in His glory (John 17).
No one can reach Heaven by natural power or goodness. Only the life of God within a person takes him to
Heaven. Heaven is a condition as well as a place. Wherever the location of Heaven, it will be where Jesus is and
under His love and protection. To really know Jesus, to have Him living within, is the only way to Heaven.
MEMORY VERSE: And this is the will of him that sent me, that every one which seeth the Son, and believeth
on him, may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day.
—John 6:40
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—1 Corinthians 15:16-34 Certainty of the Resurrection.
Tue.—1 Corinthians 15:35-58 Explanation of Resurrection.
Wed.—2 Corinthians 5:1-10 Blessings of Heaven are real.
Thu.—1 Thessalonians 5:1-11 Watching for Christ's coming.
Fri.—1 Peter 1:1-9 Hope of Heaven by Christ's Resurrection.
Devotional Reading: Philippians 3:8-21 Our bodies to be like His.
Resurrection Promised
John 6:38-40 That of all which he hath given me . . . All must come to Jesus Christ through the Father . . .
may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day. This promise from Jesus is that all the
saved will have a supernatural passage to Heaven. Salvation transforms a person from the first death to new
spiritual life in the first resurrection. There is no transformation of the spirit after the second death. Eternal life
is not obtained at death; it is received and begun in this life and continues on after death in Heaven. We must
have forgiveness of sin, or we perish eternally. The life of the lost will also go on forever; that is what makes it
so terrible. But the destiny of the lost is not what the Bible refers to as everlasting life. Everlasting life speaks
better of its quality than of its duration.
The Glory of the Resurrection
1 Corinthians 15:19-23 Now is Christ risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that
slept. Jesus was our example in all things, so we will rise from the dead as He did. Afterward they that are
Christ's at his coming.
1 Corinthians 15:35-38 Here in these verses we are told that the glory of planting a seed compares to the
Resurrection. One does not expect to get back only the seed planted, but the seed planted must die and be
quickened to come forth in a glorious manner. One seed is planted, and it dies and comes forth a more glorious
body, bearing the same grain, but with greater glory than that which was planted. How? But God giveth it a

body . . . The soul was made for God, and only God and His Spirit can satisfy it and prepare it to come forth in
glory.
The Triumph of the Resurrection
1 Corinthians 15:42-56 The dead is sown in corruption—a mortal body. It is raised in incorruption—an
immortal body. It is sown in dishonor—it goes back to the dust from which it came. It is raised in glory—
never to die again, but to go back to God Who gave it. The natural man was first, then the spiritual man. As
transformed man had an earthly body's image, so also will he have a heavenly body's image. We shall not all
sleep, but we shall all be changed. Here Paul attempts to explain the supernatural phase of the Resurrection. In
a moment—very quickly—at the last trump—no more preaching or time for preparation—for the trumpet
shall sound—awakening all that are dead, wherever their graves are. And the dead shall be raised
incorruptible—every grave will bring forth an incorruptible body and shall be changed.
After the Funeral, What Then?
1 Thessalonians 4:13-14 All of us experience death. We sorrow for departed ones. But some sorrow with
hope, some without hope. The difference is that some die in Christ, some outside of Him. If we believe . . . As
surely as Christ's death and resurrection are true facts, so also the resurrection of God's people is true. Because
He lives, we shall live also (John 14:19). Physical death is called a sleep, a sleep of the body. It is not the end of
existence. Nothing is destroyed. Death is a change, a separation of soul and body. But one thing does not change
at death—one's spiritual relationship. Those who live in Christ sleep in Jesus. Just as truly, those who live
without Him die without Him, and so without hope. By what means will God raise His people to eternal life?
Shall raise up us also by Jesus—by his Spirit that dwelleth in you. (Read 2 Corinthians 4:14 and Romans
8:11.) In the same way that He raised Jesus, by the presence of God dwelling in them. Them also which sleep
in Jesus will God bring with him. Those who died having the Spirit of Christ will go to be with Jesus. Then
Jesus will bring their spirits to be reunited with their resurrected bodies.
In these modern times some try to cover death with a screen of beauty. Some try to ignore it with pain-
killing, sleep-inducing drugs before death, flowers, music, and poetry afterward. But death remains real and
universal. God calls it an enemy in 1 Corinthians 15:26 and refers to death in Hebrews 9:27. Words of friends,
sympathy cards, and funeral sermons largely imply that the departed one will go to Heaven. But it requires
something more, something from each individual, if one is to be with God.
The Manner of the Resurrection
1 Thessalonians 4:15-18 Paul spoke by the word of the Lord. This is God's Word, not Paul's. (1) We
which are alive and remain . . . shall not prevent them which are asleep. Notice the only people spoken of
here are saints, those who have died, and those still alive at Christ's coming. Those who died in sin are not
addressed here. (2) The Lord himself shall descend—He will be seen. With a shout—He will be heard. With
the trump of God—all will be awakened. (3) The dead in Christ shall rise first. The dead saints will be
resurrected first. Then we which are alive—saints who have not yet died—shall be caught up together with
them in the clouds. Those souls who have died without Christ will not be in this supernatural reunion. The dead
in Christ from all ages shall come forth from the graves with new immortal bodies, along with those still living.
(4) Where will all go? To meet the Lord in the air, and to ever be with the Lord, eternally, time without end,
never again separated from Him. Paul was giving hope to the brethren of all ages. The wicked will be
resurrected at the same time, but to a sadly different destiny (John 5:28-29).

changed to be immortal, caught up by supernatural power to meet the supernatural Lord, and taken to dwell in a
